neighbours.label: The abstract noun in a set phrase after 'new' (new heights, new light, new era, new standards); new with a concrete thing, and these nouns alone, stay low
fire: The coach has taken the young team to new heights this year.
These letters shed new light on the poet's early life.
The treaty opened a new era of trade between the two.
Factories must follow new standards for clean water.
Her research reached new heights after the grant.
The discovery throws new light on ancient farming.
Their victory ushered in a new era for the city.
Regulators set new standards for bank capital.
quiet: The coach has bought the young team new shirts this year.
These letters sat on the poet's old desk for years.
The treaty was signed in a small room between the two.
Factories must fill new trucks with clean water.
Her fear of heights kept her away from the ladder.
The lamp throws a soft light on the kitchen table.
Their car broke down on a new road near the city.
Workers set new tables for bank staff.

short: new heights, new light, new era
